title: Texas BBQ Gets a Halal Makeover
summary:
Have you ever waited in line for something really yummy? At Goldee's BBQ in Fort Worth, Texas, people line up early—even at 6:30 in the morning! They wait for hours just to taste the barbecue.

But here's the cool part: Goldee's and other spots are serving halal barbecue. Halal means the meat is prepared in a special way that Muslims can eat. For a long time, it was hard for Muslims to find barbecue they could eat. Now, there are at least a dozen halal BBQ places in Texas!

One pitmaster, Zain Shafi, makes tandoori smoked turkey. That's a dish with spices from Pakistan. Another spot, Kafi BBQ, has a 13-spice Wagyu brisket and pomegranate-glazed beef belly burnt ends. Yum!

Salahodeen Abdul-Kafi used to work in Silicon Valley (that's a place where tech people work). He moved to Texas six years ago and started smoking brisket in his backyard. Now he owns Kafi BBQ. He says his goal is to make the best barbecue in Texas—and it doesn't have to include pork.

People are loving it. Jonathan Tate said the sausage at Kafi BBQ is "the top sausage I've ever had." Another customer, Haris Ghaffar, drove an hour just to eat at Goldee's. He said it's a "blessing" to have so many options now.

Food writer Farhan Mustafa says, "Halal food is American food." It's part of what makes America great—people bringing their own traditions and making something new. So next time you see a halal BBQ joint, give it a try!
why_it_matters: When you taste food from another culture, you learn something about your neighbors — and you may find a new favorite meal.

WHAT: New halal barbecue restaurants let Muslims enjoy Texas barbecue.
WHERE: Texas, including Goldee's BBQ in Fort Worth and Kafi BBQ.
WHY: Because traditional barbecue often could not be eaten by Muslims, and these cooks show that great Texas barbecue doesn't need pork.
